issue.title: Update: Secrets_Management_Cheat_Sheet
issue.body:
## What is missing or needs to be updated?

The Secrets Management Cheat Sheet is about 9,200 words, roughly four times the size of a typical sheet in the series. It's the largest one we have.

- Section 4, Cloud Providers (about 1,600 words), walks through AWS, GCP and Azure services one by one, including HSM and confidential computing products. That belongs in vendor docs.
- Section 10, Multi-Cloud, repeats the multi-cloud advice already in 4.1.4.
- Section 3, CI/CD (about 1,700 words), overlaps the Secrets Management section of the [CI/CD Security](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/CI_CD_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html) cheat sheet, and this sheet never links it.
- Section 2 is about 2,700 words, including two full architecture walkthroughs for automated rotation.

## How should this be resolved?

- Cut the per-vendor rundown down to how to choose a secrets store and what to require from it. Link vendor docs instead of describing each product.
- Merge section 10 into section 4.
- Decide which sheet owns CI/CD secrets guidance, keep it there, and cross-link from the other.
- Trim section 2 to the principles, and keep the rotation examples to a few sentences each.
- If the sheet is still too big after that, split the CI/CD and cloud guidance into their own short sheets.

Small PRs, one section at a time, please. They are much easier to review than one big rewrite :)

comments.body:
Hi @jmanico @mackowski  ,

I'd like to help with this issue by starting with a small PR focused on the multi-cloud section.
After reviewing the proposed cleanup, I think Section 10 could be consolidated into Section 4.1.4 (“Other clouds, Multi-cloud, and Cloud agnostic”). The goal would be to preserve any useful multi-cloud-specific guidance, remove repeated recommendations already covered elsewhere in the sheet, and keep the existing links to relevant secrets-management solutions.

I'd keep this first PR limited to that single file and leave the cloud-provider rundown, CI/CD overlap, and automated-rotation examples for separate changes, as suggested in the issue.
Does this scope align with what you had in mind for the first contribution?
Thanks!

2827.title: docs: consolidate multi-cloud secrets guidance (#2793)
2827.body:
### Description

This PR consolidates Section 10 ("Secrets Management in a Multi-Cloud Environment") into Section 4.1.4 ("Other clouds, Multi-cloud, and Cloud agnostic") of the Secrets Management Cheat Sheet, as requested in issue #2793.

- **Consolidation**: Section 10 duplicated the multi-cloud guidance from Section 4.1.4 and general controls from Section 2. The distinct operational challenges (disparate APIs, varying access control models, inconsistent rotation mechanisms, and fragmented audit logging) and key defensive controls (standardizing policies, automating rotation, and centralizing audit trails using a cloud-agnostic solution) have been cleanly incorporated into Section 4.1.4.
- **Cleanup**: Deleted the redundant Section 10 (including the mid-document `### 10.4 References` list). Renumbered `## 11 Related Cheat Sheets & further reading` to `## 10 Related Cheat Sheets & further reading` to maintain sequential numbering.
- **Scope**: Modifies a single file (`cheatsheets/Secrets_Management_Cheat_Sheet.md`). Sections 2, 3, and all other sections remain untouched.

2900.title: docs: streamline CI/CD secrets management guidance
2900.body:
## Description

This PR reduces Section 3 ("Continuous Integration (CI) and Continuous Deployment (CD)") of the Secrets Management Cheat Sheet, as requested in [[issue #2793](https://github.com/OWASP/CheatSheetSeries/issues/2793)](https://github.com/OWASP/CheatSheetSeries/issues/2793).

- **CI/CD guidance:** Removed generic pipeline hardening and security recommendations that overlap with the CI/CD Security Cheat Sheet. Added cross-references to the relevant sections.
- **Secret delivery models:** Shortened the guidance on CI/CD-stored secrets, external secrets managers, and runtime secret retrieval while preserving the key security considerations.
- **Authentication and authorization:** Retained least-privilege access, OIDC workload identity, short-lived credentials, and caller attribution.
- **Monitoring and rotation:** Focused the guidance on detecting unauthorized secret access and exfiltration, and preserving dynamic credential expiry and revocation.
- **GitOps:** Kept the guidance on encrypted secrets, environment-specific keys, and secure secret generation.
- **Scope:** Changes are limited to `cheatsheets/Secrets_Management_Cheat_Sheet.md`. Section 3 was reduced from approximately 1,719 to 726 words. Section 10 now includes a reference to the CI/CD Security Cheat Sheet.

2941.title: docs: reduce Secrets Management cheat sheet section 2
2941.body:
## Description

This PR reduces Section 2 ("General Secrets Management") of the Secrets Management Cheat Sheet, as requested in [issue #2793](https://github.com/OWASP/CheatSheetSeries/issues/2793).

- **General guidance:** Removed conversational filler and consolidated the guidance on high availability, centralization, least-privilege access, automation, auditing, resilience, policies, and metadata.
- **Automated rotation:** Removed the lengthy Kubernetes YAML example and vendor-specific implementation details. Retained two architectural patterns: dual-credential phased rotation (with cryptographic key retention) and orchestrated multi-step rotation (with safe handling of single-active credential invalidation, idempotency, and testing).
- **Secret delivery:** Clarified the distinction between secret delivery and actual credential rotation at the backing service. Sidecars are described as delivery and refresh mechanisms requiring application reload or restart, with a cross-reference to Section 5.2.
- **Memory protection:** Removed lengthy hardware side-channel discussions while preserving practical memory protection guidance, including memory dumps, swap, secure zeroing, runtime-neutral managed runtime limitations, process separation, and core dump protection.
- **Secret lifecycle:** Consolidated guidance across creation, distribution, rotation, revocation, and expiration. Categorized memorized passwords (per NIST SP 800-63 FAQ #q-b05), TOTP shared secrets, and WebAuthn credentials separately. Removed outdated password delivery recommendations involving SMS and email.
- **Transport security:** Recommended TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3 with forward secrecy and strict certificate validation, and framed mutual TLS (mTLS) for zero-trust transport-layer client identity verification.
- **Scope:** Changes are limited to `cheatsheets/Secrets_Management_Cheat_Sheet.md`. Section 2 was reduced from approximately 2,728 to 1,836 words (a 32.7% reduction). This PR handles Section 2 separately from the Section 3 changes in PR #2900.
